featured_reviews.name: Madhavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
This church isn’t just another place of worship — it’s one of the oldest in Mumbai, with origins that trace back over 400 years to the Portuguese Franciscan era. The original structure has been rebuilt multiple times, and the current building — completed in the 1970s — was redesigned by renowned architect Charles Correa, giving it a distinctive, almost modernist architectural character that sets it apart from traditional church designs. There’s even a special skylight in the baptistery designed by celebrated artist M.F. Husain, adding an artistic touch to the sacred space.

Visitors and worshippers consistently describe the church as a peaceful and reflective haven, providing a calming contrast to the busy streets outside. Many find the quiet interiors, gentle lighting, and sense of reverence deeply moving — whether they’ve come to pray or simply to sit in contemplation.

Inside during Mass, there’s often a beautiful choir and uplifting biblical artwork, which many visitors highlight as especially moving. The church’s atmosphere is welcoming to both regular parishioners and first-time visitors.

Conveniently located just a short walk from Dadar station, it’s easy to visit whether you’re a local or a traveller exploring the city’s heritage sites. The church also serves as a well-known landmark in the neighbourhood, sitting comfortably among the vibrant life of Dadar West.

Our Lady of Salvation Church is much more than a place of worship — it’s a living piece of Mumbai’s cultural and architectural history. Whether you’re drawn by its spiritual significance, curious about its design, or simply seeking a quiet moment amidst city life, it’s a highly recommended stop in Dadar.

A very silent and peaceful Shrine. The Shrine of Don Bosco's Madonna, also known as Don Bosco Church Matunga, is a famous church in Mumbai and a popular spot for Marian devotees. Construction work started with imported marble from Italy in 1954 and completed in 1957. The exterior of the church is clad with Indian granite. It contains a lot of stained glass art work also.

The Shrine is located in Matunga East, adjacent to Don Bosco School and the compound also has football, hockey, cricket, volleyball and basketball training facilities as part of the educational institutions located in the same campus.

The church is a must-visit spot for Marian devotees and is considered part of Mumbai’s heritage.

Shrine Office Timings are Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 12 noon and 2 pm to 5:30 pm, Saturday 7:00 am to 12 noon and 2pm to 6:45 pm, and Sunday 7:00 am to 12 noon. There are many masses from 6am from Sunday and evening at 6pm..

featured_reviews.name: Terence Correia
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Ignatius Church is where my faith, friendships, and fondest memories were all nurtured. It was here that I was baptized, received my First Communion, and was confirmed, milestones that marked the beginning of my spiritual journey. As a child and youth, I was an active part of the Legion of Mary and St. Anthony’s group, served as an altar server, and joined the youth and prayer groups. I loved helping with church cleaning, decorating the crib, making the Christmas star, and organizing events, all while laughing and playing around the church compound with friends who became like family.

Those days were filled with joy, service, and deep connections, memories I treasure even now. Seeing the church restored to its former glory, after more than 100 years since its foundation, fills my heart with happiness. St. Ignatius Church remains a timeless place of faith, community, and love, where every stone tells the story of generations who have grown, served, and celebrated here.

description:
The Church of Our Lady of Dolours, Wadala is a Roman Catholic church in Mumbai, India built in 1853. The parish of Our Lady of Dolours with its school, St. Joseph's was entrusted to the Salesians in 1948, about the same time as the Salesians settled in Matunga. The school was co-ed until the Salesian Sisters came into the Wadala Village with the Auxilium Convent for girls. The centerpiece of the church is a statue of the Pieta.

The parish extends till Kings Circle fly-over in the North, Naigaum, Sahakar Nagar and Kidwai Nagar in the South, Hindu Colony/Ruia College in the West and the Harbour Branch Railway line including the Reynold's Road, BPT Quarters in the East.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting Gloria Church in Byculla, Mumbai felt like discovering a gentle pause button hidden within the city. In a part of Mumbai that is constantly buzzing with movement, people, and stories, the church stands as a serene reminder that beauty doesn’t always shout—sometimes it simply waits for you to notice it.

From the moment I approached the church, I was struck by its quiet dignity. The structure rises gracefully, not trying to overpower its surroundings but still unmistakably commanding attention. Stepping inside, there was an immediate shift in energy. The air felt calmer, almost sacred, as if the space itself encouraged you to slow your pace and lower your voice—not out of obligation, but out of respect.

What stayed with me most was the sense of warmth the church offers. The soft light filtering through the windows, the gentle echo of footsteps, and the stillness of the interiors create an atmosphere that feels deeply personal. Even if you walk in as a visitor with no specific purpose, the space makes you feel welcome. I found myself sitting quietly, absorbing the calm, letting my thoughts settle—something that rarely happens in the rush of everyday life.

There’s a powerful emotional depth in Gloria Church that goes beyond its architecture. You can sense the **generations of faith, hope, and prayer** that have passed through these walls. The church feels lived-in, not in a worn-out way, but in a way that reflects continuity and care. It stands as a witness to countless personal moments—gratitude, grief, joy, and silent reflection.

What I appreciated most is how Gloria Church doesn’t demand anything from you. It simply offers space—space to reflect, to feel grounded, and to reconnect with something deeper, whether that’s faith, history, or inner peace. It’s not just a religious landmark; it’s an emotional anchor in the city.

For anyone exploring Mumbai beyond its usual landmarks, Gloria Church is worth visiting—not just to see it, but to experience it. You leave feeling calmer, more centred, and quietly grateful for spaces that still allow the soul to breathe.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar d
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gloria Church, located in Byculla, Mumbai, stands on one of the oldest Roman Catholic church sites in the city.
2.  The original church, known as Nossa Senhora da Glória, was built in 1632 by Portuguese Franciscans (with some sources crediting the deSouza e Lima family).
3.  It was initially located in Mazagaon and served the community for over three centuries.
4.  The present structure was constructed between 1911–1913 (completed in 1913) in beautiful English Gothic Revival style.
5.  The church features stunning Gothic tracery in stone-carved windows, tall spires, and intricate architectural details inspired by European cathedrals.
6.  It celebrated its centenary (100 years of the current building) in 2013.
7.  The site has a continuous history of worship spanning over 400 years, making it a significant heritage landmark.
8.  The church is famous for its vibrant stained glass windows that create colorful light effects inside during the day.
9.  It underwent major restoration and reopened in 2018, appearing even more magnificent with its 160-feet tall structure.
10.  Gloria Church remains an active parish under the Archdiocese of Bombay and is a popular spot for locals and visitors seeking peace and history.
This beautiful church continues to be a symbol of faith and Mumbai’s Portuguese colonial heritage!

featured_reviews.name: The Lone Crusader
featured_reviews.review_text: Our Lady of Salvation Church, Dadar, better known as Portuguese Church, is one of the oldest churches in Mumbai. Originally built in 1596 by the Portuguese Franciscans, the church was rebuilt several times. The modern version was conceptualized by internationally renowned architect, Charles Correa, and the late Cardinal Valerian Gracias, then the archbishop of Bombay, blessed the church and consecrated its new granite altar on Feb 2, 1977. The Heritage Cross seen outside the walls of the church on the pavement was built in the 19th century,  in the late Baroque Portuguese style. A Portuguese inscription at its base reads, Fabricada por Jacinta Barretto de Vadalla, A. D. 1885. Today, the Portuguese Church is part of the "holy trinity" of churches along the arterial roads connecting Bandra to Dadar and beyond, the other two being St. Michael's Church and Our Lady of Victories Church.

featured_reviews.name: Joseph Nunes
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Andrew’s Church, with its 400+ years of rich history, has recently undergone a transformative 20-month renovation that beautifully preserves its heritage while rejuvenating its spiritual ambiance.

✨ Architectural Revival
Façade and Roof Rejuvenation: Heritage specialists like Jivraj Sankhat and Savani Heritage Conservation expertly restored the church’s iconic roof, façade, marble, woodwork, and stained-glass windows, reviving their original splendor.

Traditional Techniques: The renovation prioritized authenticity. Over 5.5 ft thick walls were replastered with lime instead of cement—an effort to maintain the church’s historical integrity.

🌞 Rediscovered Beauty
Choir Loft & Lighting: Long-hidden architectural gems, such as the choir loft’s clerestory windows, were uncovered—reintroducing natural light into the nave and restoring a key visual element of the original design.

💒 Interior Elegance
Faithfully Restored Altars: The Portuguese-inspired altars, once scarred by moisture and termite damage, were carefully conserved and revived to their former glory.

Wooden Pulpit Revival: Carved with biblical narrative, the original pulpit was meticulously restored, complete with its ornate canopy—allowing worshippers to once more feel its spiritual resonance.

⏳ Heritage Sensitivity & Community Effort
Meticulous, Not Hasty: From April 2024 to December 2025, the renovation focused on preservation over superficial repairs—respecting the church’s Portuguese colonial architecture.

Community-Driven, Funded by Love: Entirely financed by parishioners and diaspora support, the project faced financial hurdles—yet the community’s unwavering commitment ensured the work reached its homestretch.

🎖 A Joyous Reopening
On a beautiful Sunday evening, over a thousand worshippers celebrated the church’s rededication—blessed by Cardinal Oswald Gracias—marking a poignant return to its rightful spiritual grandeur.

In summary, the recent renovations at St. Andrew’s Church masterfully balance respect for its centuries-old heritage with modern integrity. From the reimagined façade to the restored interior treasures, every detail reflects love, care, and unwavering faith. It’s a testament to what can be achieved when a community unites to preserve its legacy—and a spiritually uplifting sanctuary reborn.

featured_reviews.name: Madhavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our Lady of Remedy Church in Kandivali West is a peaceful and welcoming place that holds deep spiritual significance for the local community. The church has a calm and prayerful atmosphere, making it an ideal space for reflection, worship, and inner peace, even amidst the busy surroundings of the city.

The church is well maintained and aesthetically pleasing, with a simple yet beautiful interior that helps devotees focus on prayer. The Masses are well organized, meaningful, and conducted with devotion, making them spiritually uplifting for people of all ages. The choir and liturgy add to the reverent experience, especially during feast days and special occasions.

One of the most admirable aspects of Our Lady of Remedy Church is its strong sense of community. The parish actively engages in social, educational, and charitable activities, encouraging unity and service among parishioners. The clergy and volunteers are approachable, supportive, and dedicated to guiding the faithful.

Overall, Our Lady of Remedy Church is not just a place of worship but a spiritual home for many. It stands as a symbol of faith, hope, and togetherness in Kandivali West, and is highly recommended for anyone seeking a serene and spiritually enriching experience.

As you step inside, there’s an immediate feeling of quiet reflection and comfort. The interiors are simple yet graceful, creating a spiritual atmosphere that invites prayer and contemplation. Regular masses, novenas, and festive celebrations bring the parish community together, especially during important occasions like Christmas and the annual feast.

What makes this church truly special is the warmth of the people and the welcoming environment. Whether you visit for prayer, a special ceremony, or simply to find a moment of peace, Our Lady of Remedy Church leaves you feeling spiritually uplifted and connected.
